record.paper_title: Spin-density-functional theory: some open problems and application to inhomogeneous Heisenberg models
record.original_question: In spin-density-functional theory, where the basic output consists of spin-resolved charge densities, how can one compute physically correct equilibrium electronic currents when those currents are known to be functionals of the charge density but the required current-as-density functional is unknown, and when Kohn-Sham orbital currents from the auxiliary noninteracting system are not guaranteed to equal the true interacting-system current?

evidence.quote: From a practical point of view, among the most important tasks remaining in the development of SDFT are to obtain ever better approximations for the exchange-correlation (xc) functional, and to learn how to calculate further quantities of physical and chemical interest from the output quantities of SDFT, the spin-resolved charge densities.

Electronic currents are one example. Such currents are functionals of the charge density, but cannot be calculated as such because this functional is unknown. The current calculated from the Kohn-Sham (KS) orbitals of SDFT is that of the auxiliary noninteracting system, and not guaranteed by the basic theorems of SDFT to be the correct current.
Open problems, such as the best way to deal with currents, noncollinearity and nonuniqueness, provide fascinating challenges, but they have never stoped DFT from advancing on the practical side.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a non-relativistic system of N interacting electrons in an external scalar potential and possibly a Zeeman-type magnetic field that couples only to spin. Within spin-density-functional theory (SDFT), the fundamental variables are the spin-resolved charge densities n_↑(r) and n_↓(r) (equivalently the total density n(r) = n_↑(r) + n_↓(r) and spin magnetization m(r) = n_↑(r) − n_↓(r)). The Hohenberg–Kohn–Levy theorems for SDFT guarantee that the ground-state expectation value of any observable is a functional of (n_↑, n_↓), and the Kohn–Sham (KS) construction introduces auxiliary noninteracting orbitals {φ_iσ} reproducing the exact spin densities n_σ(r) = Σ_i |φ_iσ(r)|².

Let j(r) denote the true equilibrium electronic current density of the interacting system, and let j_KS(r) = (ℏ/2mi) Σ_{i,σ} [φ_iσ*(r) ∇φ_iσ(r) − c.c.] be the current density computed from the KS orbitals. By the SDFT Hohenberg–Kohn theorem, j is in principle a functional j[n_↑, n_↓](r), but this functional is not known explicitly, and in general j_KS ≠ j.

Problem. Devise a constructive prescription that, given as input only the spin-resolved ground-state densities (n_↑, n_↓) — or equivalently the converged KS orbitals of an SDFT calculation — produces the physically correct equilibrium current density j(r) of the interacting system. Either:
(a) exhibit an explicit (possibly approximate but systematically improvable) density functional j[n_↑, n_↓](r) and justify its correctness from the basic theorems of SDFT, or
(b) prove that under stated conditions the KS current j_KS coincides with the true current j and characterize when these conditions hold, or
(c) demonstrate rigorous bounds, identities, or correction terms relating j_KS to j that are expressible as functionals of (n_↑, n_↓).
artifact.status_search_result: Standard references and reviews on (spin-)density-functional theory continue to treat the correct evaluation of equilibrium electronic currents from spin densities as an unresolved foundational issue, typically addressed only by moving to enlarged frameworks such as current-density functional theory (CDFT) that take the paramagnetic current as an additional basic variable. No general constructive functional j[n_↑, n_↓](r) within plain SDFT has been established, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Spin in density-functional theory
status_evidence.snippet: Different options for setting up Kohn–Sham DFT schemes for open-shell systems imply different definitions of the exchange–correlation energy functional and lead to different exact conditions; the paramagnetic current density can be incorporated into extended DFT frameworks.
status_evidence.claim: Currents are typically handled only by extending SDFT to current-density functional theory; no current-as-density functional is known in plain SDFT.

status_evidence.title: The Structure of Density-Potential Mapping. Part I: Standard Density-Functional Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses ongoing foundational open questions in DFT including differentiability of the universal functional and limits of the Kohn–Sham scheme.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational questions about which observables are computable as explicit functionals of the density remain unresolved.
